the effort: Wong led the engineering team that worked on the $1,500 device, which combined a wearable computer with a display mounted at eye level and sold to developers and entrepreneurs.
According to his LinkedIn profile, he is planning to be a senior director overseeing software quality at Oculus.
But months after joining Facebook and shortly after starting at Oculus, as indicated by his LinkedIn profile, which has not been updated since Nov. 13 last year, Wong quit the company. At the time, he did not say why he was leaving Facebook in a tweet, according to a Google translation.
On Friday, Google's page for Wong reports that he became a director at Alphabet Inc. in April, but the Alphabet page for Wong is identical to his previous page at google.com.
